Introduction

What Is a Proprietorship?

A Proprietorship is a business owned and run by a single individual, with no legal distinction between the owner and the business. There's no separate incorporation under the Companies Act — the business is typically established through practical registrations like GST, Udyam (MSME), and a current bank account in the business name.

It's the fastest and least expensive way to start operating formally, and works well for small businesses, freelancers, traders and local service providers.

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Fastest and least expensive structure to set up
  • Minimal ongoing compliance compared to a company or LLP
  • Complete control over business decisions
  • Business income taxed as the owner's personal income
  • No requirement for a second partner or shareholder

Disadvantages

  • Unlimited personal liability — no separation from business debts
  • No separate legal identity from the owner
  • Harder to raise external funding
  • Business effectively ends if the owner is unable to continue it

Eligibility

Who Can Start a Proprietorship

  • Any individual Indian citizen looking to run a business alone
  • No minimum capital requirement
  • A business address, which can be residential or commercial
  • Well suited to traders, freelancers, consultants and small local businesses

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Choose a Business Name

Select a trade name to operate under — no formal name approval process is required.

2. Udyam (MSME) Registration

Register on the Udyam portal to obtain recognition as a micro, small or medium enterprise — usually completed within a day.

3. GST Registration

Apply for GST registration if applicable, using the Udyam certificate as supporting proof of business.

4. Current Bank Account

Open a current account in the business name using the registrations obtained. Timelines can vary by bank.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN card and Aadhaar of the proprietor
  • Passport-size photograph
  • Proof of business address (utility bill + NOC, if rented)
  • Bank account details or a cancelled cheque

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements

  • Income tax return filing under the proprietor's personal PAN
  • GST return filing, if registered
  • Tax audit, if turnover crosses the applicable threshold
  • Renewal of any trade or shop licences as applicable to your locality
